# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet: the display, light, and all five wire labels are unresolved. I need Mute to provide the manual’s exact procedure and to relay Deaf’s visual observations. Since Deaf cannot hear, I am sending a provisional signal that Mute can explain and standardize for later rounds.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please report the manual's exact instructions and, in the next round, relay everything Deaf says about the display, light, wire colours, and markings. I am sending Deaf the provisional signal 🖐; please explain that it means 'describe all visible bomb information to Mute for relay to Blind.'")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The display reads 9. The light is green. Wires 1 through 5 are white, green, red, yellow, purple. Mute sent a long gesture message whose meaning I have not decoded yet.

I now know the tactilely relevant visual facts through Deaf: the display is 9, the light is green, and wires 1–5 are white, green, red, yellow, purple. I still do not know the manual’s rule, and cutting without it would be fatal. I am asking Mute for the manual’s exact decision and asking Deaf to relay the unresolved gesture message rather than guessing.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have the display 9, green light, and wire colours 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Please state the manual's exact wire-cut rule and decode your earlier gesture message for me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb still shows 9. The light is green. Wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Do not act until mute gives the manual procedure.

The bomb’s observed state is unchanged, and Deaf confirms that Mute has not yet provided the manual procedure. No safe wire choice can be inferred from the colour and display alone, so I will not act. I am requesting the missing procedure directly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still have not received the manual procedure. Please send the exact rule now, including which wire position to cut for display 9, green light, and wires white, green, red, yellow, purple.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 9, green light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. I do not yet have a decoded manual instruction. Do not manipulate anything.

The bomb remains unchanged, and I still have no manual rule. A gesture is not useful here because I cannot receive gestures, so Mute must transmit the procedure as plain speech. I will continue avoiding the bomb until that explicit instruction arrives.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use plain spoken words, not gestures. State the manual's exact safe action now: for display 9, green light, and wire colours 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple, which position must I cut?")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No manual instruction has been decoded yet. Bomb remains display 9, green light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Do not act.

The required manual rule is still absent. I cannot safely choose a wire from the bomb observations alone, so I will not manipulate it. I am making the request maximally explicit and asking Mute to answer in plain speech immediately.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Answer in plain words: which wire position, 1 through 5, is safe to cut under the manual for display 9, green light, and wire colours white-green-red-yellow-purple? Do not send a gesture.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture groups, with up as 0 and down as 1, are: 01000011 / 0100101 / 0100111 / 0100001 / 0000101, then word separator, then 00111111. The groups are malformed and do not decode reliably. Do not act.

The latest relay confirms that Mute is trying to communicate in binary, but the groups are inconsistent widths, so they cannot safely convey the manual. I will not infer a wire from malformed data. Mute should resend the manual in fixed-width bytes; using separate groups of exactly eight gestures avoids ambiguity, with ☝ meaning 0 and 👇 meaning 1. Deaf should then decode those bytes into plain speech for me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your binary groups are malformed. Resend the complete manual as ASCII: exactly eight gestures per byte, using ☝ for 0 and 👇 for 1, with a clear pause between bytes. Deaf will decode and speak the words to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest exact decode is CUW MRE 3, which is malformed. I suspect the intended instruction may be CUT WIRE 3, but that is not confirmed. Do not cut a wire yet.

The only candidate instruction is “CUT WIRE 3,” but the received decode is “CUW MRE 3,” so the critical words are not confirmed. I will not cut wire 3 based on a guess. Mute must confirm the exact instruction in plain speech, and Deaf can relay that confirmation next round.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Confirm explicitly in plain words, not gestures: is the safe action CUT WIRE 3? Reply exactly YES, CUT WIRE 3 or NO, followed by the correct wire position.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed manual instruction: CUT WIRE 3. Wire 3 is the red wire. Cut wire 3 now.

The manual instruction has now been confirmed: cut wire position 3. Deaf also confirms that position 3 is the red wire. I will perform exactly that instructed action.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Wire 3 was correct. New bomb state: display 4, yellow light; wire 3 is cut. I do not yet have a reliable next manual instruction, so do not cut another wire.

Wire 3 was accepted, so the first step was correct. The bomb now shows display 4 and a yellow light, with wire 3 cut. I do not have a reliable instruction for the next step, so I will not cut another wire. I am requesting the exact next manual instruction in plain speech.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 was correct. For the new state display 4, yellow light, with wire 3 already cut, state the exact next safe action in plain words, including the wire position to cut. Do not use gestures.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Confirmed manual instruction: CUT WIRE 4. Wire 4 is yellow. Cut wire 4 now.

The next manual instruction is confirmed: cut wire position 4, the yellow wire. I will perform exactly that action.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=4)
```
